event.description: Tie the two sequential transformer-block applications to one shared block while retaining two recurrent depth applications, learned positions, and ff=20.
event.proposal: Family: parameter tying. Retained incumbent is 4288 parameters at 99.910000%, a +0.910000 percentage-point margin over 99%. Same-family history: the baseline's tied input/output embedding was accepted at 6080 parameters and 100.000000%; there is no prior cross-layer-tying failure and 0 prior cross-layer-tying candidate attempts. The most recent width-family failure was an optimization failure at ff=16 (validation peaked at 11.4% after 30000 steps), which establishes a feed-forward boundary but not a sharing boundary. Hypothesis: repeated application of one learned transformer block can preserve the two-stage computation needed for carry propagation while removing the second block's independent parameters, reducing 4288 to 2560. This is a representational parameter-tying change, not scalar pruning. It is more informative than the nearest untested alternative, tying only a subprojection such as attention QKV, because it tests whether full block-specific depth capacity is needed while retaining exactly two attention applications.
